title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
contract: Return the length of a strictly increasing subsequence. Equal values cannot extend it.
brute: int[] dp=new int[a.length];Arrays.fill(dp,1);int best=0;for(int i=0;i<a.length;i++){for(int j=0;j<i;j++)if(a[j]<a[i])dp[i]=Math.max(dp[i],dp[j]+1);best=Math.max(best,dp[i]);emit("Try every earlier predecessor","index",i,"lengths",dp);}return best;
optimal: int[] tails=new int[a.length];int size=0;for(int x:a){int lo=0,hi=size;while(lo<hi){int mid=(lo+hi)/2;if(tails[mid]<x)lo=mid+1;else hi=mid;}tails[lo]=x;if(lo==size)size++;emit("Minimize the tail for this subsequence length","value",x,"tails",Arrays.copyOf(tails,size));}return size;
reasoning: Quadratic DP stores the longest increasing subsequence ending at each index.
tails[len−1] is the smallest possible final value for any increasing subsequence of length len seen so far.
Lower-bound search replaces the first tail ≥ x; equal values replace instead of extending. The tails array is a length certificate, not necessarily a subsequence from the input.
